text:
maria_finance: Heads-up 1 Apr: new lighter approval flow for recurring SaaS under $5k/year goes live in the procurement portal. This is intended to speed approvals for small, recurring tools (monitoring, analytics, design tools).
liam_engineering: Awesome. Will this touch our Datadog/Log tools? They ramp monthly sometimes.
sara_sales: Quick Q  does this apply to credit card subscriptions already on company cards?
maria_finance: Good Qs. Short answers: 1) If the subscription is managed via the portal (recommended), it follows the new flow. If it's on a company card outside the portal, team should migrate it into procurement to be eligible. 2) For tools with rapid seat growth, set an expected growth estimate when you submit; if expected annualized cost stays < $5k, it remains auto-approved. Otherwise manual review.
procure-bot: New workflow added: "SaaS - Recurring <$5K". Auto-verify vendor, attach T&Cs snapshot, and issue single-use virtual card when needed. Missing tags (#project, #cost-center) will flag item for manual review.
olivia_legal: Note: if vendor requires e-signature or has non-standard indemnity clauses, the flow will stop and route to legal. Please flag any vendor with custom contract language.
liam_engineering: If a service has a free tier plus paid add-ons, how should we estimate the annual cost? Use expected usage?
maria_finance: Use expected paid usage across the next 12 months (conservative estimate). If uncertain, choose "pre-approval" in the portal and include a short note on assumptions.
sara_sales: Is procurement still creating POs for these? We need POs for customer-reimbursable expenses.
maria_finance: Yes 1 auto-approved subs still get a PO record and PDF snapshot. Reimbursable items that need receipts should still be routed through expense reports; procurement POs do not replace individual expense receipts.
liam_engineering: Will the portal attempt to detect vendor auto-renewals? We had an unnoticed renewal last quarter.
maria_finance: Portal will attempt detection for vendors onboarded there and will send a 30-day renewal notice to the listed owner. Please verify the owner field on existing vendor records.
procure-bot: Reminder: after rollout, procurement will run a 2-week audit of auto-approved items to validate tagging and spend estimates. Teams may be contacted for clarifications.
olivia_legal: Also reminder: any multi-year deal that averages >$5k/year or has termination fees requires manual review.
sara_sales: Thanks  can you post a one-line checklist we can paste into team onboarding guides?
maria_finance: Posted in the portal guide (link in #announcements). TL;DR: 1) Put purchase in portal 2) Add #project & #cost-center 3) Estimate annualized spend 4) Mark owner & renewal preference 5) Choose pre-approval if unsure.
liam_engineering: Great, we'll start migrating tools this week. If we find edge cases I'll open a ticket.
maria_finance: Thanks! We'll monitor first 30 days and iterate. :eyes:
